text:
Morgan: Hey team — our app started seeing 600-800ms tail latency and occasional 503s this morning. We pinned Dedicated pool to us-west for low latency, but traces show requests hitting eu-west. Any idea why?
Aisha: sorry to hear that, can you paste a sample request id or timestamp?
Morgan: yes — request_id=8f3b2c, seen at 2026-03-17T09:12:03Z. Header we set: X-Redwood-Region: us-west.
Aisha: thanks. quick checks — are you using strict_region_affinity?
Morgan: no, we left default (allow_fallback: true). We assumed "pinned" meant strictly in-region for Dedicated.
Aisha: that explains part. Default behavior allows overflow to hosted pools when dedicated capacity is saturated. Can you run:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate 
```
and include the response headers (x-redwood-route, x-redwood-hosted-fallback)?
Morgan: ran it twice, saw: x-redwood-route: eu-west-2, x-redwood-hosted-fallback: true, and latency 720ms. Also got a 503 once with body: "capacity_unavailable".
Aisha: copy. I'm going to escalate to infra — tagging @Luca and @Kai.
Luca: looking at routing logs for req 8f3b2c — router decision:
```
routing_decision: fallback_hosted=true
reason: capacity_spillover
requested_region: us-west
pinned_region: us-west
selected_host: hosted-eu-west-2
dedicated_pool_available: 0/12
```
Notably the dedicated pool shows 0 available despite metric exporters reporting some free slots. Suspect mismatch between autoscaler cooldown and router capacity accounting.
Kai: we saw similar yesterday during a burst — autoscaler scale-up lag + immediate spillover caused router to send traffic to hosted. There might be a condition where spillover_threshold is incorrectly lower during cooldown.
Aisha: Morgan — immediate mitigation options: 1) set allow_fallback=false in your route so requests are rejected instead of going to hosted (will reduce cross-region latency but cause errors if dedicated is saturated), or 2) use a stricter header X-Redwood-Region-Strict: true (temp workaround) if available. Which do you want?
Morgan: prefer option 1 for now (we'd rather fail than incur cross-region traffic). Please apply it while you investigate.
Aisha: done — set allow_fallback=false for your customer route id cust-8421. You should see failures instead of eu-west responses. Can you confirm?
Morgan: confirmed — now 503s but no eu-west routes. Thanks.
Luca: root cause hypothesis: when a dedicated pool is pinned to a region and autoscaler is in cooldown, the router's available-slot calc uses a stale cache that can go negative, triggering spillover. We'll push a hotfix to router to clamp to zero and re-evaluate upstream autoscale events.
Kai: immediate infra mitigation: increase dedicated pool min-instances and bump autoscale cooldown to 60s for affected clusters. That reduces chance of transient zero-availability.
Sophie (billing-bot): note — any requests that spilled to hosted will be billed at hosted rates. I'll open an invoice review for cust-8421.
Aisha: thanks @Sophie — please mark as "billing-review: possible-spillover-credit". Morgan we'll keep you updated. Ticket ENG-1198 created and assigned to eng-runtime.
Luca: attaching quick repro and logs for the eng-runtime fix — reproducible steps: 1) create dedicated pool with min=2 max=12 pinned to us-west, 2) send 200 concurrent requests with short interval, 3) watch router logs show "capacity_spillover" then autoscaler scale-up event 8s later.
Luca: temp router patch pushed to stage to clamp negative availability; will promote to prod after QA.
Morgan: really appreciate the fast response. Do you have ETA for permanent fix?
Luca: aiming for prod roll 3 hours after QA. Will update this thread.
Kai: postmortem checklist created — includes: fix clamp bug, add metric for "spillover_rate", add alert if spillover>0.5% per minute, and doc change to clarify "pinned" vs "strict" semantics.
Aisha: I'll follow up with Morgan once fix is live. :thumbsup:
Morgan: thanks team :pray:
